title: Elastic SLO-driven Cost Simulator and Rollout Playbook
author: Asha Kapoor
content:
Summary
-------
This design spec describes an Elastic SLO-driven Cost Simulator (ESCS) and an associated Rollout Playbook for validating, pricing, and safely deploying SLO-aware cost controls across Redwood product surfaces (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private). The ESCS helps product and engineering teams simulate the end-user economics of different SLO/route configurations, model variants, batching and caching policies, and quota bundles before a public release. The Rollout Playbook prescribes a safe, measurable sequence to introduce SLO-driven pricing and routing changes to customers.

Goals
-----
- Provide a repeatable simulation workflow that predicts per-request and per-tenant cost under configurable SLO and workload assumptions.
- Surface risk signals (latency regressions, quality drop, cost overshoot) prior to rollout.
- Enable product to iterate on pricing/packaging by running closed-loop experiments against recorded traffic traces.
- Define an operational rollout plan with canary thresholds, rollback criteria, and metrics dashboards.

Non-goals
---------
- This spec does not replace the runtime inference scheduler or the real-time routing engine.
- ESCS is not intended to be the canonical billing engine; it outputs estimates to inform pricing and experiments.

Stakeholders and Ownership
--------------------------
- Product (owner): Asha Kapoor — overall product requirements and experiment prioritization.
- Eng-Serving-Runtime: Diego Morales — simulation fidelity and model execution cost profiles.
- Eng-Platform: Lena Park — data ingestion for traces, historical workload replay infra.
- Finance: Morgan Reyes — pricing scenarios and revenue impact analysis.
- SRE/Support: rotation-based reviewers for rollout and incident response.

Success Metrics (pre-release and post-release)
---------------------------------------------
Pre-release:
1) Simulation absolute error vs. production billing <= 8% on average across baseline workloads.
2) Detects cost overshoot scenarios (>= 10% deviation) with >= 90% recall on historical data.

Post-release:
- No customer-facing latency SLO breaches attributable to rollout > 1 per 10k requests.
- Customer cost delta matches simulated estimate within +/- 12% for >= 80% of customers in the first month.

Functional Requirements
-----------------------
1. Workload Modeling
   - Support importing historical traces (request metadata, token counts, model variant id, observed latency and status).
   - Synthetic traffic generator with controls: qps, sequence length distribution, concurrency, percent of streaming vs non-streaming.
2. Cost & SLO Configuration
   - Allow definition of per-model token cost (multi-currency), batching efficiency curves, and KV cache hit rate assumptions.
   - Express SLOs as latency p50/p95/p99 and tail percentiles by route/model.
3. Simulation Engine
   - Replay mode (deterministic) and Monte Carlo mode (stochastic) for sampling workloads.
   - Produce per-tenant and aggregate metrics: tokens, GPU-seconds, queuing delay, expected bill, and projected latency percentiles.
4. Experiment Specification
   - JSON/YAML experiment manifests with variables: routing policy, quantization profile, batching window, cache TTL, and quota bundle.
5. Reporting & Alerting
   - Automatic generation of a report: summary, per-tenant projections, top 10 divergence causes, and confidence intervals.
   - Exportable CSV/JSON and dashboard seeds for Grafana.
6. Security & Data Residency
   - Support encrypted trace ingestion and per-customer data scope consistent with Private deployment policies.

Non-functional Requirements
---------------------------
- Simulation runs must complete within a target of 2 hours for a 7-day trace at 5M requests/day on standard infra.
- Modular design so new cost factors (e.g., new hardware types, accelerator pricing) can be added without rework.
- Role-based access controls for running or viewing experiments.

Design Overview
---------------
Components:
- Trace Ingest Service: normalizes historical traces into the ESCS canonical schema.
- Cost Profile Catalog: stores model execution cost curves (per-variant, per-hardware/quantization).
- Simulation Orchestrator: schedules deterministic replay and Monte Carlo experiments.
- Scenario Runner: runs config permutations in parallel, captures outputs.
- Report Generator & Dashboard Seeds: consolidates outputs and emits canonical dashboards and experiment artifacts.

Canonical Simulation Data Schema (text table)
- This table describes the canonical flat schema used by the simulator for each request record.
| field_name | type | example | notes |
| request_id | string | rq_0123 | unique |
| tenant_id | string | tnt_acme | scoping |
| timestamp | string | 2026-10-11T12:23:45Z | ISO8601 |
| route | string | /v1/chat/completions | route |
| model_variant | string | gptx-7b-fp16 | model variant id |
| tokens_in | int | 48 | input tokens |
| tokens_out | int | 512 | output tokens |
| observed_latency_ms | int | 180 | end-to-end |
| status | string | ok | ok|error|

Simulation Modes and Controls
----------------------------
1) Replay Mode: deterministic replay of historical traces. Controls: time-scale factor, concurrent worker count, preserve ordering per-tenant.
2) Monte Carlo: samples synthetic requests using a parameterized request distribution. Controls: seed, sample size, distribution knobs.
3) Param Sweep: run a grid of configurations (e.g., quantization profiles × batching window × routing policy) in parallel and compute aggregate metrics.

Pricing Scenario Examples (table)
| Scenario | Assumptions | Projected per-1M requests cost | Notes |
| Baseline (current routing) | batching=default, cache hit=8% | $1,200 | baseline for comparison |
| Aggressive-Quant | 8-bit quant, batching +20% | $680 | quality check required |
| SLO-Priority | route routed to low-latency pool, batching -15% | $1,540 | better p95 at higher cost |

Example Experiment Manifest (YAML)
---
name: slo-priority-q4-pilot
routes:
  - path: /v1/chat/completions
    routing_policy: slo-priority
    target_slo_ms: 200
model_variants:
  - id: gptx-7b-q8
    quant: q8
    cost_profile: q8-default
batching:
  window_ms: 8
  max_batch_tokens: 4096
cache:
  kv_ttl_seconds: 3600
  expected_hit_rate: 0.12
output: /experiments/slo-priority-q4-pilot/results.json
---

Rollout Playbook (step-by-step)
-------------------------------
1. Preflight (owner: Product, Eng-Serving-Runtime)
   - Run ESCS on a representative 14-day trace for top 20 tenants.
   - Validate simulation error on a holdout week <= 8%.
   - Produce experiment report and sign-off from Finance and SRE.
2. Internal Canary (owner: Eng-Platform)
   - Deploy change to internal tenant namespace (10k QPS cap) for 48 hours.
   - Monitor latency p95/p99 and error budget burn. Stop if p95 increases > 15% or errors > 0.5% absolute.
3. Customer Canary (owner: Customer Success)
   - Invite 5 pilot customers representing different workload shapes. Run for 7 days.
   - Collect billing deltas and survey product quality (NPS-like feedback).
4. Gradual Ramp (owner: Product)
   - Increase coverage 10% -> 30% -> 60% over 4 deployment waves, each wave 48–72 hours.
   - Gate between waves: simulated vs observed cost divergence <= 12% and latency within thresholds.
5. Full Rollout and Billing Migration (owner: Finance/Product)
   - Announce changes via billing portal and email 14 days prior.
   - For Dedicated/Private customers, provide migration guide and opt-out window (30 days).
6. Post-release Monitoring and Reconciliation (owner: SRE/Finance)
   - Run reconciliation job weekly for first month comparing ESCS forecast and actual usage.
   - If systemic divergence > 20% for > 3 customers, pause further rollouts and open incident review.

Canary and Rollback Criteria (thresholds)
---------------------------------------
- Immediate rollback if any of the following during a canary window:
  - p95 latency increase attributable to change > 25% absolute.
  - Error rate increase > 1% absolute and correlated with routing change.
  - Customer-reported quality regression with severity P1.
- Soft pause (investigate) if:
  - Simulated vs observed billed cost delta > 15% for multiple tenants.
  - Cache hit rate deviates from assumed > 10% absolute.

Dashboards and Key Metrics (Grafana seeds)
------------------------------------------
- ESCS Experiment Summary: projected cost vs observed cost, projected p95 vs observed p95, divergence heatmap by tenant.
- Per-Tenant Drilldown: request rate, tokens, model-variant mix, cache hit, batching efficiency, billed estimate, actual bill.
- Alerting: experiment divergence alert, canary SLA breach alert, billing-reconciliation alert.

Operational Runbooks (short)
---------------------------
- How to run a simulation: 
  1) Upload trace: curl -X POST /escs/ingest -F file=@trace.ndjson -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'
  2) Start experiment: ecsctl run --manifest slo-priority-q4-pilot.yaml --timeout 3h
  3) Fetch report: ecsctl fetch --id <exp-id> --format html
- Investigation checklist on divergence:
  1) Compare trace vs live sampling to ensure representativeness.
  2) Validate cost profile for model-variants changed recently.
  3) Check hardware mix and preemption events in the window.

Privacy, Security, and Compliance Notes
--------------------------------------
- All ingested traces must be PII-scrubbed prior to upload unless customer provides explicit consent and a private deployment.
- For Private deployments, certificates and KMS keys are used to encrypt trace exports.
- Access to the ESCS UI and experiment artifacts is RBAC-restricted to entitled roles.

Migration Guide for Dedicated/Private Customers
-----------------------------------------------
- Provide an export of simulated billing under the new SLO-prices for the last 90 days.
- Offer a 30-day opt-out for Dedicated customers; for Private, provide migration scripts and an on-prem estimator binary.

Open Questions and Risks
-----------------------
- Simulation fidelity for multi-model pipelines where cross-model KV cache interactions exist.
- How to price edge-case workloads with heavy streaming and long-lived KV sessions.
- Governance process for approving pricing changes with material revenue impact (> $250k ARR).

Appendix A — Glossary
---------------------
- ESCS: Elastic SLO-driven Cost Simulator.
- SLO: Service Level Objective.
- KV cache: key-value cache for prefix or context caching during inference.

Appendix B — Quick CLI Examples
------------------------------
# upload trace
curl -X POST \
  'https://console.redwood.example/api/escs/ingest' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -F 'file=@acme-week2.ndjson'

# launch experiment
ecsctl run --manifest slo-priority-q4-pilot.yaml --parallel 8 --output /tmp/exp-results

# reconcile results
python tools/reconcile_escs.py --exp /tmp/exp-results --window 30 --out /tmp/recon.csv
